key_insight: Video understanding requires tracking what changes and when—not just inspecting isolated frames. VIVID aims to preserve localized visual changes and evolving entity information under tight frame budgets.
problem_solved: Video MLLMs can overlook small moving objects when pooling whole frames and lose motion or event order when skipping intermediate frames or averaging tokens.
method: Use localized visual differences to emphasize changing regions rather than static backgrounds.
Represent entity dynamics textually to help track changes across time.
Connect these spatial and temporal cues for video reasoning. These approach elements are indicated by the title; the truncated abstract does not provide implementation details.
impact: This direction could make frame-budget-constrained video QA more sensitive to subtle motion and event sequences. The provided excerpt does not report measured improvements.
visual_elements: Split-screen comparison: isolated keyframes versus a connected video timeline.
Frame overlays highlighting a small moving object against a static background.
Entity timeline pairing visual changes with short textual state updates.
Motion arrows illustrating direction and event order lost when intermediate frames are skipped.
paper_title: VIVID: Beyond Static Multi-Image Reasoning with Localized Visual Differences and Textual Entity Dynamics in Video MLLMs
paper_authors: Chengqian Ma, Yuanze Zeng, Hongyu Wang, Mingfeng Lin, YiCheng Xiao
